opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Today’s readings left me thinking about two men who spoke the same truth but experienced very different endings.

Jeremiah was sent to warn Judah that their rejection of God would bring destruction. The people were furious. They wanted him put to death simply because he spoke the words God had given him. Yet Jeremiah was spared. Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, stood beside him and protected him.

Then the Gospel shifts to John the Baptist. Herod hears about Jesus and wonders if John has returned from the dead. Matthew reminds us why Herod would think such a thing. John had confronted him with the truth about his sinful life. Herodias hated John for it. A dance, a foolish promise, and a desire to save face before his guests ended with John’s head presented on a platter.

Both Jeremiah and John spoke God’s truth. One was spared. One was martyred.

At first, that seems difficult to understand. Why would God save one prophet and allow another to die?

Perhaps because God’s faithfulness is not measured by whether He rescues us from suffering. Jeremiah’s work was not yet finished. John’s was. John’s entire life pointed toward Christ, and even his death became part of that witness.

There is another thread woven through both readings. Jeremiah challenged a nation. John challenged a king. Jesus would challenge the whole world. The response was always the same: when the truth becomes uncomfortable, people often try to silence the one who speaks it.

That has never really changed.

We still resist correction. We still prefer comfortable words over difficult truths. Sometimes we even avoid the people who lovingly point us back to God because their words expose something we would rather ignore.

What struck me most was not that Jeremiah lived and John died. It was that neither man measured his mission by the outcome. They measured it by their faithfulness. They simply spoke what God had entrusted to them.

I wonder if that is what God asks of us as well. Not that we always be successful. Not that life always be easy. But that we remain faithful to the truth He has placed within our hearts.

Yesterday, Jeremiah taught me that the Potter simply tries again with the clay. Today, Jeremiah and John remind me that once the vessel begins to take shape, it must also have the courage to be used.

Lord, give me the courage to speak truth with humility, to receive truth with an open heart, and to trust that whether You ask me to persevere, to wait, or to suffer, You are never absent. Help me to be faithful, and leave the outcome in Your hands.
